public_rationale: OpenAI's announcement confirms the financing event Marcus cites: $6.6 billion raised at a $157 billion valuation. That supports the factual basis of his investor admission. It does not settle whether his technical and economic predictions were largely correct. The relevant prediction set and its outcome record remain insufficiently established. There is no demonstrated contradictory component that would justify a mixed verdict.
limitations: Only the financing component is independently established here.
An expression of uncertainty is not equivalent to a categorical failed prediction.

our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that most of the relevant prior technical and economic predictions held through 2024, while investor willingness to finance OpenAI exceeded his expectations.
The surrounding text identifies examples and a possible core set, but does not clearly close the set of predictions covered by this overall assessment.
The investor example concerns a financing valuation above $150 billion, not a funding amount of $150 billion.
I assess the retrospective through calendar 2024. I do not use later outcomes to score predictions as though they had already occurred.
This is a claim about his forecasting record, so the contract has no company financial metric. The funding evidence carries its own financial scope.
criteria.support_condition: A documented inventory of the relevant earlier predictions, assessed consistently against outcomes through 2024, shows that most held; independent financing records also confirm the outcome he identifies as exceeding his expectations.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A consistently assessed inventory shows that most relevant predictions failed, or independent records refute the financing outcome underlying the investor admission.
